tasks.title: Secrets in .env.production (Stripe both modes, Chatwoot, mail)

prep.what: Populate .env.production on the server with all runtime secrets: Stripe test+live keys, Chatwoot API token, and SMTP mail credentials.
prep.understand: `.env.production` is never committed to git. It needs four Stripe keys (test publishable + secret, live publishable + secret), the Chatwoot base URL + API token, and your SMTP host/user/password. Missing or wrong keys will cause hard failures at runtime. Run `php artisan config:cache` after to bake them in and verify nothing is missing.
approach: SSH into azteam-vps; locate or create `.env.production` (copy from `.env.example` as a scaffold).
Fill Stripe keys from the Stripe Dashboard (both test and live modes).
Fill Chatwoot API token from the Chatwoot settings panel; fill mail creds from your SMTP provider.
Run `php artisan config:cache` and check for any missing-key errors before moving on.

tasks.title: Scheduler safety guard: cutover_completed flag blocks minting pre-reconcile
tasks.notes: spec §7 step 2. Add settings.cutover_completed (bool, default false); RunRecurringBilling::handle() bails+logs if false.

prep.what: Add a `cutover_completed` boolean to the DB settings table (default `false`); make `RunRecurringBilling::handle()` bail with a log entry if the flag is false.
prep.understand: This is a one-time safety gate: the scheduler must not mint any recurring billing before reconciliation (t39) is confirmed. The flag must live in the DB (not `.env`) so it survives `config:cache`. A bail is not a silent skip — it must log a warning so you can see it happened.
approach: Add `cutover_completed` (boolean, default false) to the `settings` table via a migration.
At the top of `RunRecurringBilling::handle()`, read the flag; if false, `Log::warning('RunRecurringBilling: skipped, cutover not completed')` and return.
Write a unit test: instantiate the job with `cutover_completed = false`, assert it returns without minting and logs the warning.
Confirm the flag survives `php artisan config:cache` (it reads from DB at runtime, not config files).

tasks.title: Reconciliation gate: imported AR + recurring state matches azteam_crm ground truth
tasks.notes: Reconciliation gate BLOCKS go-live. CrmImporter::reconcile() (~line 277) computes per-client + TOTAL open-AR. Extract to ReconciliationGateService + artisan command billing:reconcile-cutover.

prep.what: Extract `CrmImporter::reconcile()` into a standalone `ReconciliationGateService`, add an artisan command `billing:reconcile-cutover`, run it against production data, and confirm zero delta before deploying.
prep.understand: Reconciliation compares your new billing system's open-AR totals against the legacy `azteam_crm` DB as ground truth. Any mismatch = abort go-live. The gate must be reproducible (a named artisan command) and produce a clear pass/fail + delta report. It's read-only — zero writes during this step.
approach: Extract the logic from `CrmImporter::reconcile()` (~line 277) into `App\Services\ReconciliationGateService` with a `run(): ReconciliationResult` method.
Add `php artisan billing:reconcile-cutover` that calls the service and prints per-client deltas + a PASS/FAIL summary.
Run it against production data (read-only connection); review any deltas.
Only proceed to t36 deploy if the command exits PASS — zero delta on every client and TOTAL.

tasks.title: DO droplet deploy (app/queue/scheduler/TLS/MySQL8, scheduler OFF)
tasks.notes: LEMP on azteam-vps → https://fin.azteam.cloud. php8.4-fpm + supervisor queue:work + cron. Docker stack was reverted. Scheduler must remain OFF.

prep.what: Deploy the full LEMP stack to azteam-vps: git pull + build, MySQL8 migration, supervisor queue worker, nginx + TLS cert for fin.azteam.cloud — with the scheduler intentionally OFF.
prep.understand: This is bare-metal LEMP (php8.4-fpm + nginx + MySQL8 + supervisor). Docker was tried and reverted — do NOT reintroduce it. Deploy order matters: DB first (migrate), then app build, then supervisor for queue:work, then nginx+TLS. Scheduler cron must NOT be added yet — that's t40 after reconciliation.
approach: SSH into azteam-vps; `git pull origin main && composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader && npm run build`.
Run `php artisan migrate --force` to apply the DB schema; verify tables look correct.

Configure supervisor (`/etc/supervisor/conf.d/azteamai-worker.conf`) for `php artisan queue:work --sleep=3 --tries=3`; `supervisorctl reread && supervisorctl update && supervisorctl start azteamai-worker`.
Configure nginx server block for `fin.azteam.cloud`; run `certbot --nginx -d fin.azteam.cloud` for TLS; verify HTTPS loads the app.
Confirm `php artisan schedule:run` is NOT in crontab yet (scheduler OFF). Check `.env.production` `APP_URL=https://fin.azteam.cloud`.

tasks.title: Enable scheduler; watch first run; register Stripe webhook LAST
tasks.notes: Enable scheduler AFTER reconciliation passes; flip cutover_completed flag; register Stripe webhook LAST (URL must match APP_URL, HTTPS only).

prep.what: Flip `cutover_completed = true`, add the Laravel scheduler to crontab, watch the first run in logs, then register the Stripe webhook as the final step.
prep.understand: Order is critical: set flag first → enable cron → watch logs → register webhook. The webhook URL MUST be HTTPS and match `APP_URL` exactly (fin.azteam.cloud). Registering the webhook before the app is stable could trigger billing events you're not ready to handle.
approach: `php artisan tinker` → `\App\Models\Setting::set('cutover_completed', true)` (or however your settings model works).
Add cron entry: `* * * * * cd /var/www/azteamai && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1`.
Watch `storage/logs/laravel.log` for the first scheduler run; confirm `RunRecurringBilling` fires and logs a run (not a bail).
Register the Stripe webhook in the Stripe Dashboard: URL = `https://fin.azteam.cloud/webhooks/stripe`, events = `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`, `customer.subscription.*`.

tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine + DB guard
tasks.notes: Guard foundation done (PendingOutbound model + DB checks). Net-new: full state transition logic (pending→approved/rejected/expired) + approval endpoint.

prep.what: Complete the `PendingOutbound` approval state machine: implement the state transitions (pending → approved / rejected / expired), an expiry job, and the API endpoint that processes approvals.
prep.understand: The DB foundation is already done (commit `f8740ce`): the model, `approvalTokenHash`, `expiresAt`, `consumedAt`, `approvedByUserId` FK, and DB CHECK constraints exist. What's missing is the behavior layer: who can transition which states, the guard that prevents double-consume, expiry cleanup, and the endpoint. This is security-critical — only authorized users may approve agent-generated outbound messages.
approach: Define state transitions in an `ApprovalService`: `approve(token, user)` — verify token hash + not expired + not consumed, check user has approval permission, set status+consumedAt+approvedByUserId; `reject(token, user)` — same guards, set rejected status; `expire()` — bulk-set expired on overdue rows.
Add a scheduled job (or artisan command) that calls `ApprovalService::expire()` on rows past `expiresAt`.
Add a `POST /api/outbound/{id}/approve` endpoint with auth middleware; call `ApprovalService::approve()`; return 200 or 422 with reason.
Add feature tests: approve with valid token → 200; double-approve → 422; expired token → 422; unauthorized user → 403.

tasks.title: Append-only audit log for privileged agent actions
tasks.notes: ActivityLog model + lib/activity-log.ts exist (generic, tenant-scoped). Net-new: agent-specific fields, append-only enforcement, breach-detector pattern hooks.

prep.what: Extend the existing `ActivityLog` into a true append-only audit trail for privileged agent actions — adding agent-specific fields, enforcing no-delete/no-update at the DB level, and wiring it into the breach-detector query path.
prep.understand: The foundation exists (`ActivityLog` model + `lib/activity-log.ts` — generic, tenant-scoped). Net-new: recording `agentId`, `actionType`, `policyDecision`, and `affectedResourceIds` per privileged action; DB-level append-only constraint (trigger or policy that blocks DELETE/UPDATE on committed rows); and a query helper the breach detector can use to find anomalous patterns (e.g. high-volume agent actions, repeated policy rejections).
approach: Add agent-specific columns to `activity_logs` via migration: `agent_id` (FK nullable), `action_type` (enum/string), `policy_decision` (enum: allowed/denied/flagged), `resource_ids` (JSON array).
Add a DB trigger (or application-level guard) that raises an error on DELETE or UPDATE of any `activity_logs` row — making it append-only.
Update `lib/activity-log.ts` to accept and persist the new fields when recording privileged agent actions; wire it into the agent action dispatch path.
Add a `AuditLogQuery` helper with methods like `suspiciousActions(tenantId, window)` that returns anomalous patterns for the breach detector.
